## Projection parameters

```{r projtable}


df <- data.frame(nsims = 500, years = 30)

ft <- flextable(df) |>
    fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") |>
    font(fontname = "Arial", part = "all") |>
    set_caption(
      align_with_table = FALSE,
      word_stylename = "Normal") |>
    width(j = 1:ncol(df), width = c(1, 1))

ft <- set_caption(
    ft,
    caption = flextable::as_paragraph(
      as_chunk("Table 1. Projection parameters",
               props = fp_text(italic = FALSE)
      )
    ),
    align_with_table = FALSE
  )

ft

```

## Quinsam/Cambpell


### Input parameters

```{r QCtable}

get_OMtable(pop = "qc", caption = "Table 2. Input parameters for the projection model for Quinsam and Campbell Rivers, specifying the class where they are applied (Biological = Bio, Hatchery, or Harvest) and the parameter source. When parameters are drawn the posterior of the conditioning model, median values and interquartile range are provided here for reference, but the full posterior distributions are used in the projections. For time-varying paratmeters, the time-period over which the paratmeter is averaged is specified. See conditioning model results for uncertainty distributions of parameters at-age, and more details on posterior distributions.") 

```

### Outputs


Contour plots of performance metrics from projections of Quinsam/Campbell Chinook along a gradient in hatchery releases as a proportion of most recent five-year average (x-axis) and a gradient in pre-terminal exploitation rates (y-axis). Performance metrics  are median values among Monte Carlo trials for the last year of the projection: proportionate natural influence (PNI), total catch, abundance of natural spawners, abundance of returns, pre-terminal catch, terminal catch, total hatchery-origin catch, and total natural-origin catch. Dashed lines represent the recent 5-year average pre-terminal exploitation rate (horizontal) and hatchery release (vertical, set to 1.0), and the solid horizontal line is the pre-terminal exploitation that when combined with the recent 5-year average terminal exploitation rate results in a combined exploitation equal to the aggregate *U<sub>MSY</sub>* for natural-dominated populations.



```{r QCfig, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "QC", "gic1_QC.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "QC", "gic2_QC.png"))

```


#### Key messages

- Spawner abundances and returns increase as pre-terminal exploitation rates decline.

- Catches are maximized above MSY exploitation rates, except for terminal catches which are maximized at relatively low exploitation rates where spawner abundances are high.

- Spawner abundances, returns, and catches increase with hatchery releases.

- PNI declines with increases in pre-terminal ERs as spawner abundances decline, and PNI declines with increases in hatchery releases. A change from the current designation of "Integrated Hatchery" (PNI <0.5) to "Integrated Transition" (PNI<0.8 and >=0.5) could occur with reductions in hatchery releases to < 75% of current levels, and pre-terminal ERs < 15%.


```{r QCtradeoff, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "QC", "gto3_QC.png"))

```

### Trade-off plots

The relationship between spawner abundances and catches can be illustrated in a trade-off plot including various combinations of pre-terminal ERs (colours) and hatchery production (symbols, binned into 6 groups). Catches are maximized at intermediate pre-terminal exploitation rates and high hatchery production, and spawner abundances are maximized at low pre-terminal exploitation and high hatchery production.

## Nimpkish


### Input parameters

```{r Nimpkishtable}

get_OMtable(pop = "nimpkish", caption = "Table 3. Input parameters for the projection model for Nimpkish River, specifying the class where they are applied (Biological = Bio, Hatchery, or Harvest) and the parameter source. When parameters are drawn the posterior of the conditioning model, median values and interquartile range are provided here for reference, but the full posterior distributions are used in the projections. For time-varying paratmeters, the time-period over which the paratmeter is averaged is specified. See conditioning model results for uncertainty distributions of parameters at-age, and more details on posterior distributions.") 

```


### Outputs

Contour plots of performance metrics from projections of Nimpkish Chinook along a gradient in hatchery releases as a proportion of most recent five-year average (x-axis) and a gradient in pre-terminal exploitation rates (y-axis). Performance metrics  are median values among Monte Carlo trials for the last year of the projection: abundance of natural spawners, abundance of returns, probability that natural spawners are greater than *S<sub>gen</sub>*, probability that natural spawners are greater than 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>*, proportionate natural influence (PNI), total catch, pre-terminal catch, terminal catch, total hatchery-origin catch, and total natural-origin catch. Dashed lines represent the recent 5-year average pre-terminal exploitation rate (horizontal) and hatchery release (vertical, set to 1.0), and the solid horizontal line is the pre-terminal exploitation that when combined with the recent 5-year average terminal exploitation rate results in a combined exploitation equal to the aggregate *U<sub>MSY</sub>* for natural-dominated populations.

#### Key messages

- Spawner abundances and returns increase as pre-terminal exploitation rates decline.

- There is a high probability (0.66-0.89) that spawner abundances are above *S<sub>gen</sub>* at current pre-terminal ER and hatchery release levels. 

- There is a moderate probability (0.34-0.65) that spawner abundances are above 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>* at current pre-terminal ER and hatchery release levels. 

- Catches tend to be maximized at pre-terminal ERs higher than MSY exploitation rates, except for terminal catches which are maximized at relatively low exploitation rates where spawner abundances are high.

- Spawner abundances, returns, and catches increase with hatchery releases.

- PNI declines with increases in pre-terminal ER as spawner abundances decline, and with increased hatchery releases. A drop from "Integrated Wild" (PNI>=0.8) to "Integrated Transition" (PNI<0.8 and >=0.5) designation is expected to occur when hatchery releases are > ~175% of current levels and pre-terminal ERs are >40%. 


```{r Nimpkishfig, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Nimpkish", "gic1_Nimpkish.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Nimpkish", "gic2_Nimpkish.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Nimpkish", "gic3_Nimpkish.png"))

```

### Trade-off plots

The relationship between spawner abundances and PNI can be illustrated in a trade-off plot including various combinations of pre-terminal ERs (colours) and hatchery production (symbols, binned into 6 groups).  Abundances are projected to be greater than  *S<sub>gen</sub>* (vertical dotted line) when pre-terminal ERs are approximately <0.42, and above 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>* (vertical dot-dashed line) when pre-terminal ERs are approximately <0.3, though hatchery production also impacts abundances. It is possible to maintain PNI > 0.8 under most scenarios, except when hatchery production is > 150% of current production and pre-terminal ERs are >40%.

```{r NimpkishTradeOff, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Nimpkish", "gto_Nimpkish.png"))

```

High catches above the historical median (dashed vertical line) and high PNI (above 0.8, dashed horizontal line) occur at intermediate to high pre-terminal ERs and hatchery releases < 150% of current levels.


```{r NimpkishTradeOff2, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Nimpkish", "gto2_Nimpkish.png"))

```

High aggregate catches (above historical median) and high spawner abundances (above 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>*) occur for intermediate pre-terminal ERs (~20-30%) and moderate to high hatchery releases (>100%). 


```{r NimpkishTradeOff3, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Nimpkish", "gto3_Nimpkish.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Nimpkish", "gto3_close_Nimpkish.png"))

```


## Salmon


### Input parameters

```{r Salmontable}

get_OMtable(pop = "Salmon", caption = "Table 4. Input parameters for the projection model for Salmon River, specifying the class where they are applied (Biological = Bio, Hatchery, or Harvest) and the parameter source. When parameters are drawn the posterior of the conditioning model, median values and interquartile range are provided here for reference, but the full posterior distributions are used in the projections. For time-varying paratmeters, the time-period over which the paratmeter is averaged is specified. See conditioning model results for uncertainty distributions of parameters at-age, and more details on posterior distributions.") 

```


### Outputs

Contour plots of performance metrics from projections of Salmon River Chinook salmon along a gradient in hatchery releases as a proportion of most recent five-year average (x-axis) and a gradient in pre-terminal exploitation rates (y-axis). Performance metrics  are median values among Monte Carlo trials for the last year of the projection: abundance of natural spawners, abundance of returns, probability that natural spawners are greater than *S<sub>gen</sub>*, probability that natural spawners are greater than 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>*, proportionate natural influence (PNI), total catch, pre-terminal catch, terminal catch, total hatchery-origin catch, and total natural-origin catch. Dashed lines represent the recent 5-year average pre-terminal exploitation rate (horizontal) and hatchery release (vertical, set to 1.0), and the solid horizontal line is the pre-terminal exploitation that when combined with the recent 5-year average terminal exploitation rate results in a combined exploitation equal to the aggregrate *U<sub>MSY</sub>* for natural-dominated populations.


#### Key messages

- Spawner abundances and returns increase as pre-terminal exploitation rates decline.

- There is a high probability (0.66-0.89) that spawner abundances are above *S<sub>gen</sub>* and above  above 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>* at current pre-terminal ER and hatchery release levels

- Catches tend to be maximized above MSY exploitation rates, except for terminal catches which are maximized at relatively low exploitation rates where spawner abundances are high.

- Spawner abundances, returns, and catches increase with hatchery releases.

- PNI is consistently above 0.8.


```{r Salmonfig, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Salmon", "gic1_Salmon.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Salmon", "gic2_Salmon.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Salmon", "gic3_Salmon.png"))

```

### Trade-off plots

For Salmon River, catches tend to be maximized and natural spawner abundances minimized at high pre-terminal ERs, with hatchery production having relatively little impact on catch.  PNI is highest under low hatchery production, but all scenarios were >0.8. Natural spawners were consistently above *S<sub>gen</sub>* (vertical dotted line) and 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>* (vertical dot-dashed line). 
. 
```{r SalmonTradeOff, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Salmon", "gto_Salmon.png"))

```

```{r SalmonTradeOff2, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Salmon", "gto2_Salmon.png"))

```

```{r SalmonTradeOf3, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Salmon", "gto3_Salmon.png"))

```


## Adam


### Input parameters

```{r Adamtable}

get_OMtable(pop = "Adam", caption = "Table 5. Input parameters for the projection model for Salmon River, specifying the class where they are applied (Biological = Bio, Hatchery, or Harvest) and the parameter source. When parameters are drawn the posterior of the conditioning model, median values and interquartile range are provided here for reference, but the full posterior distributions are used in the projections. For time-varying paratmeters, the time-period over which the paratmeter is averaged is specified. See conditioning model results for uncertainty distributions of parameters at-age, and more details on posterior distributions.") 

```


### Outputs

Contour plots of performance metrics from projections of Adam River Chinook salmon along a gradient in hatchery releases as a proportion of most recent five-year average (x-axis, shown for consistency among populations even though there are no hatchery releases into the Adam River) and a gradient in pre-terminal exploitation rates (y-axis). Performance metrics  are median values among Monte Carlo trials for the last year of the projection: abundance of natural spawners, abundance of returns, probability that natural spawners are greater than *S<sub>gen</sub>*, probability that natural spawners are greater than 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>*,  total catch, pre-terminal catch, and terminal catch. Dashed lines represent the recent 5-year average pre-terminal exploitation rate (horizontal) and hatchery release (vertical, set to 1.0), and the solid horizontal line is the pre-terminal exploitation that when combined with the recent 5-year average terminal exploitation rate results in a combined exploitation equal to the aggregate *U<sub>MSY</sub>* for natural-dominated populations.


#### Key messages

- There are no hatchery releases into the Adam River, so performance metrics do not with hatchery size.

- Spawner abundances and returns increase as pre-terminal exploitation rates decline.

- There is a moderate probability (0.34-0.65) that spawner abundances are above *S<sub>gen</sub>* and 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>* at current pre-terminal ER. 

- Catches tend to be maximized near MSY exploitation rates, except for terminal catches which are maximized at relatively low exploitation rates where spawner abundances are high.


```{r Adamfig, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Adam", "gic1_Adam.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Adam", "gic2_Adam.png"))

```

### Trade-off plots

For Adam River, catches tend to be maximized and natural spawner abundances minimized at high pre-terminal ERs, with hatchery production having relatively little impact on catch.  PNI is highest under low hatchery production, but all scenarios were >0.8. Natural spawners were consistently above *S<sub>gen</sub>* (vertical dotted line) and 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>* (vertical dot-dashed line). 
. 
```{r AdamTradeOff, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Adam", "gto3_Adam.png"))

```

## Aggregate results


### Outputs: Base case

Contour plots of performance metrics from projections summed over populations (total populations= sum of Quinsam/Campbell, Nimpkish, Salmon and Adam River, and natural-dominated populations = sum of Nimpkish, Salmon and Adam Rivers) along a gradient in hatchery releases as a proportion of most recent five-year average (x-axis) and a gradient in pre-terminal exploitation rates (y-axis). Performance metrics are median values among Monte Carlo trials for the last year of the projection: abundance of natural spawners (all populations), natural spawners (natural-dominated populations), probability that natural spawners are greater than Sgen (summed over natural dominated populations), probability that natural spawners are greater than 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>* (summed over natural-dominated populations), total catch, total returns, pre-terminal catch, terminal catch, natural-origin catch and hatchery-origin catch. Dashed lines represent the recent 5-year average pre-terminal exploitation rate (horizontal, averaged over populations) and hatchery release (vertical, set to 1.0), and the solid horizontal line is the total *U<sub>MSY</sub>* for natural-dominated populations for pre-terminal and terminal exploitation combined.



#### Key messages

- Spawner abundances and returns increase as pre-terminal exploitation rates decline.

- There is a very high probability (0.9-1.0) that spawner abundances of natural-dominated populations are above *S<sub>gen</sub>* at current pre-terminal ER and hatchery release levels. 

- There is a high probability (0.66-0.89) that spawner abundances of natural-dominated populations are above 85% *S<sub>MSY</sub>* at current pre-terminal ER and hatchery release levels. 

- Catches tend to be maximized near or above MSY exploitation rates, except for terminal catches which are maximized at relatively low exploitation rates where spawner abundances are high.

- Spawner abundances, returns, and catches increase with hatchery releases.



```{r Aggfig, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Aggregate", "gic1_Agg.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Aggregate", "gic2_Agg.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Aggregate", "gic3_Agg.png"))

```

### Trade-off Plots

Increasing pre-terminal ER from 0 to 38% result in increasing aggregate catch over all populations, but reduced spawner abundances to natural-dominated populations. However, spawner abundances remained above aggregate Sgen (vertical dotted line) and 85% SMSY (vertical dot-dashed line), until pre-terminal exploitation exceeded 48%. Increasing hatchery production resulted in increased catch and to a lesser extent, spawner abundances. Median aggregate catch from 2002-2024 is shown with the vertical dashed line. Black diamond is the projected natural spawner abundances and aggregate catch at current pre-terminal exploitation rates and hatchery releases.<!--CH comment: why is catch maximized at 38%, when UMSY = 32%? Is this becuase of hatchery contribution, allowing higher harvest? Am running simulations with zero hatch now)-->



```{r Aggfig_tradeoff1, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Aggregate", "gto3_Agg.png"))


```



```{r Aggfig_tradeoff2, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Aggregate", "gto5_Agg.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Aggregate", "gto5_Agg_close.png"))

```



```{r Aggfig_tradeoff3, fig.cap = ""}

knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "SMSE", "Aggregate", "gto6.png"))

```
